children: Australian shares fell on Wednesday, with banks leading broad-based losses a day after the country's central bank raised interest rates to an 18-year high, while investors awaited the outcome of the US midterm elections.

Consumer-facing sectors including discretionary (.AXDJ), staples (.AXSJ) and real estate (.AXRE) stocks each fell more than 0.5%, giving back some of the gains made in the previous session.

While the Reserve Bank of Australia raised rates by 25 basis points on Tuesday, its removal of a reference to further increases was interpreted by many as a sign the tightening cycle may be nearing an end. Even so, borrowing costs remain at their highest in nearly two decades, posing challenges for consumer-facing sectors.
